answer: For labels such as nadir, ferrous, or wharf, identity verification can require a Wesolowski time-lock: each claimant performs a prescribed chain of modular squarings, where every result depends on the previous one. Clones may run on separate GPUs, but parallel hardware cannot skip steps or shorten an individual chain’s dependency path. This enforces a physical time cost per identity, while a compact proof lets verifiers check completion efficiently.
